fixes.explanation: I see why that picture comes to mind, bread floating off across the water. But the verse never mentions a far land. It says "…after many days you will find it again." (Ecclesiastes 11:1) Finding it again is the promise.
Yes, sow! "He who watches the wind will fail to sow…" (Ecclesiastes 11:4) Planting is the job, and watching the wind isn't planting. Meanwhile my dough has never risen from being stared at.

I see why travel fits with wind, but that's not the word. The verse says, "He who watches the wind will fail to sow…" (Ecclesiastes 11:4) Sowing is the work that doesn't get done. The verse says nothing about a trip.

That's it, baker! "…and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap." (Ecclesiastes 11:4) The first man fails to sow, and this one fails to reap. Sowing and reaping are the two jobs, and watching the sky doesn't get either one done.

Selling is a good guess in a farming picture, but the Teacher doesn't say it. The line is, "…and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap." (Ecclesiastes 11:4) The cloud-watcher misses the reaping, the harvest itself. Selling never comes up in the verse.

Building isn't in this verse, friend. The Teacher stays with farm work: "…and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap." (Ecclesiastes 11:4) Sowing and reaping are the two jobs he names here. Barns and building never come up.

Maker, yes! "…the work of God, the Maker of all things." (Ecclesiastes 11:5) All things, not just some things. The Teacher puts the wind and the womb right next to it. And I live on a cookie planet made just for my baking, so I know a little about being given a place by Someone else.

Keeper sounds nice, but it isn't the word here, baker. The Teacher says, "…the work of God, the Maker of all things." (Ecclesiastes 11:5) God is called the Maker of all things. That's the word the verse uses.

Yes! The Teacher says, "Sow your seed in the morning, and do not rest your hands in the evening, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper." (Ecclesiastes 11:6) Since you can't tell which sowing will work out, you keep planting. That's why I keep stamping batch after batch, friend.

Rejoice, that's the word! "So if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all." (Ecclesiastes 11:8) Not some of them, all of them. I spent years stuck in the back of a junk drawer, and I'm telling you, I rejoice a lot more now.
